assignments.reason: Direction: replace-the-torch-path-with-a-fused-flyd. The canonical kernel is still the pure-torch reference. According to report §1 and §4.1, it takes 16–63 ms per call against aiter's 0.18–2.46 ms, a mean speedup of about 0.016. Its 186–627 torch kernels per call go to dequantizing every expert's weights to bf16 (12.5 ms, independent of n_tokens), torch MXFP4 activation quantization, per-slab weight gathers and glue code. All 25 cases need the same structural rewrite into a fused FlyDSL a4w4 MoE: route and sort, quantize x to MXFP4, stage 1 (gate+up, clamped SwiGLU, MXFP4 requantization), then stage 2 (down projection times the routing weight), all on the 16x16-preshuffled weights and never materializing bf16 weights. This specialist owns the overall dataflow, the stage split and launch count, the sort/padding layout, the per-regime dispatch inside the functools.cache compile function, and the AKLR ABI rules: no output allocation, no sync, fixed-order reduction for determinism.

assignments.reason: Direction: replace-the-torch-path-with-a-fused-flyd (memory datapath of the fused kernel for the S regime). In this regime (report §3, §4.3; this is analytic modelling, not counters, because PMC is unavailable), aiter already streams about 0.97 GB of MXFP4 weights at 5.1–5.4 TB/s, 81–86% of the read roof. The ceiling over the baseline is therefore only 1.16–1.24×. In the fused kernel these 20 cases are won or lost on reading the weights: 16-byte vectorized loads from the 16x16-preshuffled fp4 weights and E8M0 scales, BM=32 tiles matched to the sort unit, one weight sweep per expert, and non-temporal versus cached loads. Weights should go straight to VGPRs, gathered A rows should come in with buffer loads, and the grid must fill the CUs, so the design has to reach about 1.03× here.

assignments.reason: Direction: replace-the-torch-path-with-a-fused-flyd (compute path for the M and L regimes). According to report §1 and §4.3, aiter is 2–7× off its roof floor at n_tokens 3112–32768. Only a native scaled MXFP4×MXFP4 MFMA design can use that gap; a bf16-dequant MFMA design ties or loses. In the candidate, torch _mxfp4 quantization (18–38% of the time) and glue dominate. This specialist owns the gfx950 scaled fp4 MFMA choice (32x32x64 vs 16x16x128), register and accumulator budgets, the MFMA/load schedule for BM=128–256 tiles, and fusing x quantization and the stage-1 clamped-SwiGLU MXFP4 requantization epilogue into vectorized per-lane code.
